record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let a graph be obtained as a limit of a network of thin tubes or guides joined at junctions, and let a nonlinear Schrödinger equation be posed on the shrinking tube system before the limit is taken. Does the vanishing-transverse-size limit produce a nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the limiting graph, and if so, which vertex boundary conditions appear at the junction? More specifically, how do the limiting vertex conditions depend on the way the tubes and junction are shrunk and on the boundary conditions imposed on the tube walls, such as Neumann or Dirichlet conditions?

evidence.quote: The graph should be a limit in some sense of a more realistic systems of thin tubes (or guides) connecting at junctions. A first problem is getting the limit of a certain dynamical model, e.g. NLS equation defined on the system of thin guides when transversal size of tube vanishes. It is reasonable to conjecture that this limit should be a NLS on a graph as defined before, but with which boundary conditions? And how the boundary conditions at the vertex could depend on the limit process of shrinking the tubes, guides and junction size? A further difficulty could be the dependence of limit process on the conditions at the boundary of the thin tube, e.g. Neumann or Dirichlet.

These problems have been tackled, with partial solution, in the linear case (see [29, 30, 31] and reference therein). They remain open for nonlinear models, where there is no literature, with the only exception (to the knowledge of the present author) of a series of papers about the reduction of the Ginzburg-Landau equation and its stationary counterpart from thin tubes to graphs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a metric graph $\mathcal{G}$ realized as the singular limit of a family $\{\Omega_\varepsilon\}_{\varepsilon>0}$ of three-dimensional (or two-dimensional) "fat" domains consisting of thin tubes of transverse size $\varepsilon$ glued at junction regions, the tubes shrinking to the edges of $\mathcal{G}$ and the junctions to its vertices as $\varepsilon\to 0$. On each $\Omega_\varepsilon$ pose the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi_\varepsilon = -\Delta \psi_\varepsilon + \kappa\,|\psi_\varepsilon|^{2\sigma}\psi_\varepsilon \quad\text{in } \Omega_\varepsilon, $$
with prescribed boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega_\varepsilon$ (for instance, Neumann or Dirichlet on the lateral walls of the tubes), where $\kappa\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\sigma>0$ are fixed.

(a) Show (or determine the conditions under which it is true) that as $\varepsilon\to 0$ suitably rescaled solutions $\psi_\varepsilon$ converge to a function $\psi$ defined on the metric graph $\mathcal{G}$, and that $\psi$ satisfies a nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi + \kappa'\,|\psi|^{2\sigma}\psi \quad \text{on each edge of } \mathcal{G}, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the edgewise Laplacian and the wave function satisfies certain self-adjoint vertex (matching) conditions at every vertex $v$ of $\mathcal{G}$.

(b) Identify which family of self-adjoint vertex conditions (e.g., Kirchhoff/standard, $\delta$-type, $\delta'$-type, decoupled Dirichlet, or more general $U(d_v)$-parametrized couplings, where $d_v$ is the degree of $v$) is selected in the limit, and characterize the dependence of these vertex conditions on:
   (i) the geometry and rate of shrinking of the junction relative to the tubes (e.g., relative scaling of junction volume vs.\ tube cross-section);
   (ii) the boundary condition imposed on the lateral walls of the tubes (Neumann vs.\ Dirichlet, or mixed);
   (iii) the nonlinearity exponent $\sigma$ and sign of $\kappa$.
artifact.category_tag: NLS on metric graphs / thin-tube limits
artifact.status_search_result: In the linear setting, the thin-tube approximation problem is well-developed: any self-adjoint vertex coupling on a quantum graph can be approximated by Schrödinger operators on shrinking branched manifolds (e.g., Exner–Post-type results). For the genuinely nonlinear NLS case, however, only partial and model-specific results exist (Ginzburg–Landau reductions, transparent vertex conditions for solitons in Y-junctions and tubular networks studied numerically/heuristically). A full rigorous derivation of NLS on a metric graph as the vanishing-transverse-size limit of NLS on fat graphs, together with classification of the resulting vertex conditions in terms of junction geometry and lateral boundary conditions, does not appear to be available; the problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: A General Approximation of Quantum Graph Vertex Couplings by Scaled Schrödinger Operators on Thin Branched Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Any self-adjoint coupling in a quantum graph vertex can be approximated by a family of magnetic Schrödinger operators on a tubular network built over the graph.
status_evidence.claim: Linear thin-tube approximation of vertex couplings is established.

status_evidence.title: Soliton transport in tubular networks: transmission at vertices in the shrinking limit
status_evidence.snippet: NLSE solved on finite thickness ('fat') graphs; dependence of solution and reflection at vertices on graph thickness studied as thickness goes to zero.
status_evidence.claim: Nonlinear case studied numerically/heuristically; rigorous limit not established.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the thin-tube limit for NLS on graphs as an open problem outside Ginzburg–Landau reductions.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in the nonlinear regime.
